title: Three Years and One Short Plan
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：treasure　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 treasure 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1987 the planner ① found the treasure that no citizen in the district would have counted, and he said the finding was the whole of the year. The ② treasure, meaning the riches itself and not the plan, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a treasure, he said, is the only thing in a district that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ treasure in that district had the same short plan beside it, and the ④ treasure at the far square, meaning the plot they kept for the children to measure and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A treasure, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the planner said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the treasure was the whole of the matter, meaning the value and not the riches. The ⑥ treasure, meaning the value and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; treasure, he said, is either something you find or the only word that means both a riches and a value. He said the value is the part they remember.

By 1992 the ⑦ treasure had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short plan. The ⑧ treasure of the whole thing, the planner wrote in March, was one district and three years of counting; treasure, he said, is either the plot at the far square or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ treasure I remember is the riches counted in the report, which closed in 1994 and is still counted as the quietest in the district. A ⑩ treasure, my mother said in 1996, is the only riches that improves by being counted; every treasure, she said, is a value that has agreed to look like a riches. She said the value was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 财宝；珍品（指街区里每一箱旁边的那一箱）
B. n. 财宝；珍品（指那箱财宝本身，与薄薄的图纸相对）
C. 固定搭配：find the treasure 寻这一箱财宝
D. n. 财宝；珍品（指留给孩子们丈量的那一块）
E. n. 财宝之事（抽象总称，指一处街区的财宝之事）
F. n. 财宝；珍品（指规划报告里写到、被清点的那一箱）
G. n. 财宝、价值（指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 价值（抽象总称，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: found the treasure that no citizen in the district would have counted
The treasure, meaning the riches itself and not the plan
the treasure at the far square
the treasure was the whole of the matter
the treasure had become a line in a report
The treasure of the whole thing
A treasure, my mother said in 1996

answers.why: find the treasure 意为“寻这一箱财宝”，1987 年那位规划员把街区里没有一位市民肯清点的一箱财宝做了一遍。
treasure 意为“财宝；珍品”，指那箱财宝本身而不是薄薄的图纸，它经过了三个年份而在簿子上没有被清点。
treasure 意为“财宝；珍品”，指街区里每一箱旁边的那一箱，每一箱旁边都有同一张薄薄的图纸。
treasure 意为“财宝；珍品”，指最远那处广场的留给孩子们丈量的那一块，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
treasure 意为“财宝、价值”，指一件事里人人都用却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这箱价值就是那件事的全部。
treasure 意为“价值”，指人人都用却无人提起的那样东西而不是那箱财宝，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
treasure 意为“财宝；珍品”，指规划报告里写到、被清点的那一箱，到 1992 年这一箱成了规划报告里的一行。
treasure 意为“财宝之事”，规划员三月写道，整件事的财宝之事是一处街区和三个年份的清点。
treasure 意为“财宝；珍品”，我记得的是规划报告里清点过的那一箱，1994 年落成了，至今仍被说成街区里最安静的一箱。
treasure 为抽象总称，母亲 1996 年说，财宝是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的财宝。
